chunks: And it is narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,
"that whoever kills a soul without [its being for] a soul or corruption in the earth, it is as though he has killed all mankind"
He said: "It is a valley in Jahannam; if he were to kill all mankind, he would be in it, and if he were to kill one soul, he would be in it."

key_terms.النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا: All mankind; used to express the enormity of the crime
key_terms.فَسَادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ: Corruption in the land; a grave crime that can warrant legal punishment
key_terms.نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ: A soul killed without lawful retaliation for another soul
key_terms.وَادٍ فِي جَهَنَّمَ: A valley in Hell mentioned as the place of punishment

ai.seo_question: What does the verse ‘whoever kills a soul, it is as if he killed all mankind’ mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the gravity of unlawful killing in the verse by describing a valley in Jahannam for the murderer. It emphasizes that killing even a single soul unjustly carries an immense moral and eschatological consequence, reflecting the sanctity of human life.
